result.summary: The viewer, playing as a neutral attacker in a blue shirt, receives the ball under pressure and makes a simple layoff. The play then moves away from him, and he does not make a significant supporting run before his team loses possession.

observations.title: Receiving With Back to Goal
observations.body: You receive the ball in the center circle with your back to the opponent's goal. A defender immediately closes you down from behind, applying pressure as soon as the pass is played.

observations.title: Secure Layoff Pass
observations.body: You make a one-touch layoff to a supporting teammate to your left. This is a good decision to keep possession under pressure rather than attempting a risky turn.

observations.title: Limited Movement After Passing
observations.body: After your layoff, your movement is a slow jog forward. You don't make a run to create a passing option for the new ball carrier or attack the space behind the defence, which keeps you disconnected from the developing attack on the wing.

observations.title: Recovery Pace in Transition
observations.body: When your team loses possession around 00:08, you are in a central position. As the opposition begins to counter-attack, your recovery is a jog rather than a sprint back into a defensive shape.
